blocks.text: ReDoS exploits regular expressions that backtrack exponentially or polynomially on crafted input. A single request can pin a CPU core for seconds or minutes and, on single-threaded runtimes such as Node.js, block every other request. Typical causes are nested quantifiers, overlapping alternation and unbounded repetition followed by a failing suffix.

items: Validation patterns for email, URL, username, date and password fields
WAF and routing rules, input sanitisers and Markdown/HTML parsers
Server-side search, filtering and log-processing patterns
User-supplied regular expressions (search, rule and filter features)
Client-side validation in the browser (impacts only the user, but can be chained)
Regexes inside dependencies (look at CVEs in npm, PyPI and RubyGems libraries)

blocks.text: Find the regex or the feature that uses one. Send increasing input lengths (for example 10, 20, 30, 40 repetitions) and measure response time; exponential growth is the signature. Always use a small cap and a unique request marker, and test only against systems you own because this class degrades availability. Use static analysers (`safe-regex`, `rxxr2`, `recheck`) on a regex in source you are allowed to read. Report the pattern, the input family and the measured time curve.
See `redos-payloads.txt` for input families that trigger classic vulnerable patterns, and generation commands. Use short lengths and stop at the first clear slowdown.

files.name: redos-payloads.txt

sections.label: Email validators with nested groups (for example ^([a-zA-Z0-9])(([\-.]|[_]+)?([a-zA-Z0-9]+))*(@){1}...)
URL validators with nested repeating groups
Whitespace and line-ending patterns (\s*\n? , \s+$ after a failed suffix)
Trailing whitespace trim vulnerability (^\s+|\s+$ in older libraries)
Quote/escape patterns ("(\\.|[^"])*" with an unterminated quote)
HTML/Markdown patterns (unclosed tags, nested emphasis, repeated brackets)
Polynomial (quadratic) cases, such as .*.*= or \s*,\s* with many separators
User-supplied regex probes (search or filter features that compile input as a pattern; use short inputs and a timeout)
Regex features that increase risk (look for these in source review)

# Input families. Increase the repetition count gradually and watch the response time; stop at the first clear slowdown.

# Generation commands (replace N with 10, 20, 25, 30, 35)
python3 -c "print('a'*N + '!')"

python3 -c "print('a'*N + 'b')"

# User-supplied regex probes (search or filter features that compile input as a pattern; use short inputs and a timeout)
(a+)+$
(a*)*$
(a|aa)+$
(a|a?)+$
(.*a){20}
^(([a-z])+.)+[A-Z]([a-z])+$
^(a+)+$
(x+x+)+y

# Regex features that increase risk (look for these in source review)
# nested quantifiers: (a+)+  (a*)*  (a+)*  (a{1,})+
# alternation with overlap: (a|aa)+  (a|a?)+  (.|\s)*
# adjacent unbounded repeats: \d+\d+  .*.*  \s*\s*
# backreferences with a quantified group
# no anchors combined with a leading .*

# Static analysis commands
npx recheck "<regex>"
npx safe-regex "<regex>"
python3 -c "import re;print(re.compile(r'<regex>'))"
semgrep --config p/redos .
